# Immunology & Inflammation M&A Target Screen: 38 Candidates for a Large-Cap Pharma Facing 2028–2030 LOE

## Executive Summary

**The immunology M&A market is at its most active in a decade.** Large-cap pharma executed 14 strategic immunology acquisitions totaling over \$97 billion between 2024 and Q2 2025, led by Johnson & Johnson (7 deals, \$33.5 billion), Sanofi (3 deals, \$12.3 billion), Novartis (7 transactions, \$11 billion), and Eli Lilly (4 deals, \$8 billion) [[7]](https://dealforma.com/large-cap-biopharma-ma-2024-q2-2025/). The immunology market itself is projected to grow from \$103.2 billion (2024) to \$257.4 billion by 2032 at an 11.8–13.6% CAGR [[4]](https://www.biospace.com/deals/top-i-i-deals-so-far-in-2024).

**This screen identifies 38 active, unacquired candidates** spanning eight mechanism-based clusters: CD19/B-cell reset cell therapies, oral TYK2/JAK next-generation agents, cytokine/receptor bispecific monoclonal antibodies, mast cell/KIT pathway assets, complement inhibitors, FcRn antagonists, novel oral peptides, and in vivo CAR-T platforms. Roughly 23 assets have been acquired since 2023 and are excluded as closed deals.

**The ten highest-priority targets**, in ranked order, span deal values from \$500 million to \$15 billion and include one Phase 3/NDA-stage TYK2 inhibitor approaching regulatory submission, two CAR-T platforms with active or imminent BLA pathways, one FcRn antagonist with a motivated parent-company seller, and a first-in-class mast-cell depleting antibody in Phase 3. Each target is profiled below with modality, pipeline depth, strategic fit rationale, deal feasibility assessment, and ballpark deal size at a reasonable acquisition premium.

## Acquirer Profile & LOE Context

The screen is calibrated to a large-cap pharma with an immunology franchise facing biosimilar or competitive pressure on flagship products in 2028–2030. The four most directly fitting acquirer archetypes based on publicly documented M&A appetite are:

- **AbbVie**: Skyrizi (risankizumab) and Rinvoq (upadacitinib) face competitive and eventual biosimilar pressure; Humira (adalimumab) biosimilar competition is already materially accelerating revenue replacement needs [[3]](https://patents.google.com/patent/US12692303). Already acquired Capstan Therapeutics for up to \$2.1 billion (June 2025, in vivo anti-CD19 CAR-T via tLNP delivery) [[7]](https://dealforma.com/large-cap-biopharma-ma-2024-q2-2025/), indicating active B-cell depletion gap-filling strategy.
- **J&J (Janssen)**: Stelara (ustekinumab) biosimilars entered the US market; next-generation immunology portfolio (Tremfya, icotrokinra) is in place but the company executed 7 acquisitions totaling \$33.5 billion upfront in 2024–Q2 2025 [[7]](https://dealforma.com/large-cap-biopharma-ma-2024-q2-2025/) and is reportedly in active acquisition discussions for Protagonist Therapeutics (market cap \$9.45 billion, March 2026) [[1]](https://www.protagonist-inc.com/product-pipeline).
- **Sanofi**: Dupixent (dupilumab) peak sales estimated 2028–2031; Sanofi executed three immunology deals at \$12.3 billion upfront in 2024–Q2 2025 [[7]](https://dealforma.com/large-cap-biopharma-ma-2024-q2-2025/), including the \$9.5 billion July 2025 Blueprint Medicines acquisition and a \$1.7 billion partnership with Earendil Labs for AI-discovered bispecific antibodies targeting Crohn's disease [[6]](https://dealforma.com/autoimmune-rd-partnerships-ma-and-venture-funding-h1-2025-review/) [[9]](https://www.labiotech.eu/best-biotech/immunology-inflammation-deals/).
- **Pfizer**: Xeljanz LOE and JAK safety overhang; seeking TYK2/oral precision immunology replacement.

The acquirer's five therapeutic gap themes are: (1) IL-17/IL-23 alternatives, (2) JAK/TYK2 next-generation oral agents, (3) B-cell reset/CAR-T cell therapy, (4) BAFF/APRIL/cytokine bispecifics, (5) upstream mast cell/complement inhibitors.

### 2. Celldex Therapeutics (CLDX) — Fit: A | Deal: \$3.5–5.5B

**Barzolvolimab is the only Phase 3-stage anti-KIT mast cell depleting antibody, with 71% complete response at 52 weeks and multi-indication Phase 2 pipeline addressing conditions with unmet need across all Th2-mediated diseases simultaneously.**

CDX-0159 (barzolvolimab) targets KIT receptor kinase, eliminating mast cells at their root. In Phase 2 chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU): 71% of patients on 150 mg Q4W achieved complete response at Week 52, with rapid improvement by Week 1 and deepening through 52 weeks across omalizumab-experienced, refractory, and naïve populations [[94]](https://ir.celldex.com/news-releases/news-release-details/celldex-therapeutics-presents-landmark-52-week-results). The global Phase 3 program (EMBARQ-CSU1 and EMBARQ-CSU2) enrolled over 1,800 patients (approximately 915 per trial) from July 2024, comparing 150 mg Q4W (loading 300 mg) and 300 mg Q8W (loading 450 mg) against placebo over 52 weeks [[92]](https://www.biospace.com/celldex-therapeutics-initiates-global-phase-3-program-for-barzolvolimab-in-patients-with-chronic-spontaneous-urticaria) [[93]](https://ir.celldex.com/news-releases/news-release-details/celldex-therapeutics-initiates-global-phase-3-program).

The Phase 2 program extends to four additional indications: chronic inducible urticaria (CIndU, Phase 2 met all primary and secondary endpoints with high statistical significance, October 2024; Phase 3 planned [[95]](https://ir.celldex.com/news-releases/news-release-details/celldex-announces-barzolvolimab-met-all-primary-and-secondary)); prurigo nodosus (Phase 2 initiated May 2024, 120 patients [[96]](https://ir.celldex.com/news-releases/news-release-details/celldex-announces-first-patient-dosed-phase-2-study-2)); eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE, Phase 2, approximately 75 patients enrolled [[90]](https://www.biospace.com/celldex-reports-second-quarter-2024-financial-results-and-provides-corporate-update)); and atopic dermatitis (Phase 2, designated fifth indication May 2024 [[90]](https://www.biospace.com/celldex-reports-second-quarter-2024-financial-results-and-provides-corporate-update)). A bispecific extension, CDX-622 (TSLP + SCF dual blocking), completed IND-enabling activities and entered Phase 1 in healthy volunteers [[90]](https://www.biospace.com/celldex-reports-second-quarter-2024-financial-results-and-provides-corporate-update).

The company held \$802.3 million in cash as of Q2 2024, with runway into 2027 [[90]](https://www.biospace.com/celldex-reports-second-quarter-2024-financial-results-and-provides-corporate-update). Wall Street consensus assigns 135% upside [[91]](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/indices/DOWG/pressreleases/29154373/can-this-growth-stock-deliver-135-upside-in-2025/). No partnership lock-ups restrict the KIT franchise. The mast cell mechanism is upstream of both the IgE/omalizumab pathway and the IL-4/IL-13/dupilumab pathway — an acquirer with Dupixent LOE exposure gains a platform that overlaps but does not cannibalize existing assets.

**Strategic fit**: Celldex is the most capital-efficient, near-term commercialization opportunity in this screen. Phase 3 data in CSU expected 2025–2026, with multi-indication Phase 2 pipeline across CIndU, PN, EoE, and AD. Comparable precedent: Sanofi's \$9.5 billion Blueprint Medicines acquisition of avapritinib/pralsetinib validated KIT inhibition as a commercial priority.

### 3. Kyverna Therapeutics (KYTX) — Fit: A | Deal: \$2–3.5B

**Kyverna is the only CAR-T company with a rolling BLA actively in submission and RMAT designation, creating both the most advanced regulatory position and the most urgent acquisition window given a 12–15 month cash runway.**

KYV-101 (miv-cel) is an autologous CD19 chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy using a fully human Hu19-CD828Z construct. Rolling BLA submission in stiff person syndrome (SPS) was initiated in August 2026 [[82]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1994702/000119312526152835/0001193125-26-152835.txt). Clinical evidence includes a case report of a patient with SPS who achieved over 100% increase in walking speed (from less than 50 meters to over 6 kilometers) within 3 months, maintained at 6-month follow-up [[53]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/PMC13042968). In a seven-patient SLE cohort, all achieved DORIS remission at 24 weeks and all became immunosuppressant/glucocorticoid-free following CAR-T infusion [[53]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/PMC13042968). No Grade ≥3 CRS or ICANS was observed [[53]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/PMC13042968).

Phase 2 programs are active in myasthenia gravis (MG) — 52-week data presented April 2026 at AAN, with a manufacturing agreement announced June 27, 2026 with ElevateBio supporting commercial-scale production [[82]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1994702/000119312526152835/0001193125-26-152835.txt); lupus nephritis (Phase 1/2, US and Germany); systemic sclerosis (Phase 1/2); and rheumatoid arthritis (COMPARE trial, data at EULAR June 2026 showing substantial reduction in ACPA-positive, treatment-refractory RA) [[82]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1994702/000119312526152835/0001193125-26-152835.txt). The company received RMAT designation for non-active secondary progressive multiple sclerosis in Q2 2026 [[82]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1994702/000119312526152835/0001193125-26-152835.txt).

The Ingenui-T manufacturing platform enables vein-to-vein CAR-T production from a whole blood draw (no apheresis required) [[52]](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.01.24.576713), with a 100% manufacturing success rate across 20 autoimmune disease patients [[52]](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.01.24.576713). Second-generation allogeneic derivative programs are in development via an Intellia Therapeutics partnership [[82]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1994702/000119312526152835/0001193125-26-152835.txt).

Ownership is widely distributed: Gilead Sciences 6.8%, Vida Ventures 7.9%, Westlake BioPartners 7.7%, Fred E. Cohen 7.5%, Bain Capital Life Sciences 5.1%, Northpond Ventures 5.7%, GordonMD Global Investments 5.1%, all executive officers and directors as a group 17.6% [[82]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1994702/000119312526152835/0001193125-26-152835.txt). CEO Warner Biddle owns 1.8% [[82]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1994702/000119312526152835/0001193125-26-152835.txt), a modest stake that typically correlates with openness to strategic transactions. No poison pill is in place [[82]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1994702/000119312526152835/0001193125-26-152835.txt).

**Cash pressure of 12–15 months creates a defined acquisition window, while BLA rolling submission in SPS substantially de-risks the lead program.** An acquirer completing due diligence by Q4 2026 can potentially close ahead of an independent FDA decision, capturing the full franchise value at a Phase 2/BLA premium rather than a post-approval multiple.

### 9. Priovant Therapeutics / Roivant Sciences — Fit: B+ | Deal: \$1.5–3B

**LISRAYA (brepocitinib) received FDA approval on August 27, 2026 — the first oral targeted therapy for dermatomyositis — making it an immediately monetizable asset with a definable peak sales trajectory and an established Roivant divestiture playbook.**

Brepocitinib is an oral dual selective inhibitor of TYK2 and JAK1, suppressing type I IFN, type II IFN, IL-6, IL-12, and IL-23 signaling [[30]](https://investor.roivant.com/news-releases/news-release-details/priovant-announces-fda-acceptance-and-priority-review-new-drug) [[73]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1635088/000114036126007447/ef20066998_ex99-1.htm). The Phase 3 VALOR study (NCT05437263, 241 participants, 1:1:1 to brepocitinib 30 mg, 15 mg, or placebo) met its primary endpoint (Myositis Total Improvement Score at Week 52) with statistically significant improvement for the 30 mg dose, with benefit observed as early as Week 4 and sustained through Week 52 [[30]](https://investor.roivant.com/news-releases/news-release-details/priovant-announces-fda-acceptance-and-priority-review-new-drug) [[72]](https://reachmd.com/news/fda-accepts-brepocitinib-nda-priority-review-assigned-for-dermatomyositis/2485898/) [[73]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1635088/000114036126007447/ef20066998_ex99-1.htm). Over 66% of patients achieved TIS ≥40 (twice the minimum clinically important difference), and over 50% achieved TIS ≥40 while achieving steroid dependency ≤2.5 mg/day [[30]](https://investor.roivant.com/news-releases/news-release-details/priovant-announces-fda-acceptance-and-priority-review-new-drug) [[73]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1635088/000114036126007447/ef20066998_ex99-1.htm). All nine key secondary endpoints were met [[72]](https://reachmd.com/news/fda-accepts-brepocitinib-nda-priority-review-assigned-for-dermatomyositis/2485898/). Safety database exceeds 2,000 patients across all studies [[30]](https://investor.roivant.com/news-releases/news-release-details/priovant-announces-fda-acceptance-and-priority-review-new-drug). Wholesale list price is \$35,000 for a 30-day supply [[75]](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/fda-priovant-pfizer-lisraya-brepocitinib-approved/829021/).

Additional pipeline programs: Phase 3 non-infectious uveitis (ongoing); Phase 2 cutaneous sarcoidosis (positive Phase 2 data announced February 2026 per StockTitan [[31]](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ROIV/priovant-announces-positive-phase-2-results-for-brepocitinib-in-ts0tl5que5vd.html), Phase 3 planned for 2026) [[30]](https://investor.roivant.com/news-releases/news-release-details/priovant-announces-fda-acceptance-and-priority-review-new-drug) [[73]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1635088/000114036126007447/ef20066998_ex99-1.htm).

Pfizer holds residual rights that create some structural complexity in a third-party acquisition. Roivant's operational model — incubate, approve, divest — makes Priovant the logical next sale following Telavant (\$7.1 billion, Roche) and Dermavant (Organon, up to \$950 million milestones plus royalties) [[102]](https://dcf-analysis.com/products/roiv-swot-analysis). ### Cluster 1: CD19/B-Cell Reset Cell Therapies — 9 Active Targets

The dominant theme in 2025–2026 immunology M&A is B-cell depletion via cell therapy, driven by proof-of-concept data from the University of Erlangen (15 patients with severe refractory SLE, inflammatory myositis, and systemic sclerosis achieving drug-free remission [[68]](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2308917) [[51]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/PMC12730949)) and the commercial success of CAR-T in oncology (J&J/Legend CARVYKTI: \$963 million 2024 revenue, 93% YoY growth [[59]](https://visionlifesciences.com/insights/car-t-cell-therapy-market-licensing)). Over 119 registered clinical trials are investigating CAR-T in autoimmune diseases as of April 2026 [[69]](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1853170/full) [[60]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/PMC13260344).

**Active targets in this cluster**: Kyverna (KYV-101, autologous CD19, Phase 2/BLA), Cartesian (Descartes-08, mRNA BCMA, Phase 3), Cabaletta (CABA-201, autologous CD19, Phase 1/2), Nkarta (NKX019, allogeneic CD19 CAR-NK, Phase 1/2), Allogene (cema-cel, allogeneic CD19, Phase 2; ALLO-329 dual CD19/CD70, Phase 1 planned), CRISPR Therapeutics CTX112 (allogeneic, Phase 1/2 oncology + Phase 1 SLE), TG Therapeutics Azer-cel (allogeneic CD19, Phase 1 autoimmune/progressive MS), and Vor Bio (telitacicept BAFF/APRIL, Phase 3). Approximately 65% of all autoimmune CAR-T trials target CD19 [[67]](https://nonabio.com/biologics-blog/car-t-cells-in-autoimmune-diseases-a-new-therapeutic-frontier/).

**Rationale for acquirer**: B-cell reset via single-dose CAR-T achieves a paradigm shift from chronic dosing biologics to disease-modifying curative intent. Acquirers who do not secure a cell therapy platform by 2027–2028 will face a structural competitive disadvantage as Phase 3 approvals (Kyverna SPS, Cartesian MG) create commercial anchors for the next generation of immunology franchises.

### Cluster 2: Oral Small Molecules — TYK2/JAK Next-Generation — 5 Active Targets

BMS's deucravacitinib (SOTYKTU) validated oral TYK2 as a commercial class with favorable safety vs. broad JAK inhibitors. The acquirer needs a second-generation oral TYK2 with superior PASI-100 data (envudeucitinib) or a first-approved TYK2/JAK1 in rare disease (brepocitinib/LISRAYA). **Key targets**: Alumis envudeucitinib (TYK2, Phase 3/NDA), Priovant brepocitinib (TYK2/JAK1, FDA-approved DM), Arcus small molecule oral inflammation pipeline (AB102 MRGPRX2, TNF TNFR1 inhibitor, CCR6, STAT6, CD40L — all pre-clinical to entering Phase 1 [[14]](https://investors.arcusbio.com/investors-and-media/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Arcus-Biosciences-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-and-Provides-a-Pipeline-Update/default.aspx) [[15]](https://investors.arcusbio.com/investors-and-media/press-releases/press-release-details/2025/Arcus-Provides-Update-on-Phase-3-STAR-221-Study-and-Concentrates-Its-RD-Investment-on-Casdatifan-and-Emerging-Inflammation-and-Immunology-Portfolio/default.aspx)), Landos omilancor (LANCL2, Phase 2 UC), and ImageneBio IMG-004 (non-covalent BTK inhibitor, Phase 1 complete [[26]](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/inmagene-receives-fda-ind-clearance-for-a-third-generation-btk-inhibitor-targeting-immunological-diseases-301547448.html)).

### Cluster 3: Cytokine/Receptor Bispecific mAbs — IL-17, BAFF, APRIL, IL-33, IL-7R — 7 Active Targets

The natural evolution from monospecific biologics, bispecific cytokine blockers simultaneously address two pathogenic axes. **Key targets**: Zura Bio tibulizumab (IL-17A+BAFF bispecific, Phase 2), Vor Bio telitacicept (BAFF+APRIL, Phase 3), Immunovant IMVT-1402 (FcRn, Phase 3), Belenos BEL512 (TSLP+IL-13, Phase 2 China), Belenos BEL536 (OX40L+IL-13, Phase 1 starting Q1 2026 [[41]](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/belenos-pipeline-updates-first-clinical-data-from-lead-asset-bel512-a-long-lasting-bispecific-targeting-tslp-and-il-13-second-asset-bel536-a-first-in-class-long-acting-bispecific-targeting-ox40l-and-il-13-phase-1-to-start-1q2026)), Zymeworks ZW1528 (IL-33+IL-4RA, preclinical [[39]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/PMC12705614)), and Aclaris ATI-052 (TSLP+IL-4R, Phase 1a/1b [[40]](https://www.delveinsight.com/blog/tslp-inhibitors-landscape)).

**Key targets**: Protagonist Therapeutics icotrokinra (oral IL-23R peptide, FDA-approved March 2026 as Icotyde for psoriasis, Phase 3 IBD ICONIC-UC/ICONIC-CD both initiated Q4 2025; LICENSED TO J&J — estimated peak sales >$10 billion [[1]](https://www.protagonist-inc.com/product-pipeline)) and PN-881 (oral IL-17A antagonist peptide, Phase 1 initiated Q4 2025 [[1]](https://www.protagonist-inc.com/product-pipeline)). ## Deal Feasibility — Ownership, Governance & Signal Analysis

Across the top-10 priority targets, four distinct deal feasibility profiles emerge:

**Profile A — Near-Term Urgency (Cash Pressure + Distributed Ownership)**: Kyverna (\$199.4M cash, 12–15 months, no single holder >8% [[82]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1994702/000119312526152835/0001193125-26-152835.txt)), Cabaletta (cash pressure, distributed VC base), Nkarta (\$182.8M cash, 16–18 months, insider selling by CEO [[83]](https://platform.valyu.ai/data-sources/valyu/valyu-insider-transactions-US/characteristics)), and Cartesian (insider selling by CEO and CFO [[86]](https://platform.valyu.ai/data-sources/valyu/valyu-insider-transactions-US/characteristics), CVR overhang) all face defined financing windows that incentivize seller receptivity to premium offers before a further dilutive capital raise.

**Profile B — Motivated Parent Seller**: Immunovant (Roivant 57% ownership, documented Vant-divestiture model) and Priovant (Roivant 75% ownership, post-approval) can be transacted via a Roivant-led process. The acquirer negotiates primarily with Roivant and then tenders for the remaining public float — cleaner and faster than an unsolicited public tender.

**Profile C — Strategic Transition Signal**: Zura Bio (new CEO January 2026, new CBO May 2026, Samsara 13D filing) and Alumis (Samsara 5.3% passive stake, IPO-stage VC cap table) both exhibit signals of companies entering a strategic maturity phase. New leadership appointments in commercial biotech typically precede exit or partnership within 18–30 months.

**Profile D — Complex Structure Requiring Pre-Negotiation**: Vor Bio (China rights carve-out with RemeGen), Protagonist (J&J pre-emption likely), and Arcus (Gilead partnership options on inflammation assets) require counterparty negotiation before an acquisition can close. These should be approached as relationship-first processes rather than unsolicited offers.

**Takeover defense landscape**: No poison pills were identified in Kyverna, Alumis, or Cartesian proxy statements [[82]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1994702/000119312526152835/0001193125-26-152835.txt) [[100]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1699737/000169973725000027/0001699737-25-000027.txt) [[85]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1453687/000145368726000064/0001453687-26-000064.txt). Standard Delaware law protections apply. The Zura Bio 19.99% blocker held by AI Biotechnology (Blavatnik) could serve as a practical (though not contractual) acquisition impediment if not addressed with Blavatnik first.

**Partnership lock-ups**: The most significant encumbrance in the universe is Protagonist's J&J license on icotrokinra — functionally, J&J has de facto right of first negotiation on any acquisition. Allogene's Servier EU/UK rights (signed Q1 2024, covering all EU Member States and United Kingdom for cema-cel [[110]](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/allogene-therapeutics-reports-first-quarter-200100464.html)) would require Servier consent or assignment fees in an acquisition. All other top-10 targets have clean deal structures with no disclosed blocking partnerships on their lead assets.

## Key Conclusions for BD Decision-Making

**The window for sub-\$5 billion Phase 3/NDA-stage deals is narrowing.** Alumis (NDA planned Q4 2026), Kyverna (BLA rolling submission Aug 2026), and Cartesian (Phase 3 AURORA ongoing) are advancing toward approval milestones that will structurally re-rate their market capitalizations. Pre-approval acquisitions at Phase 3 premiums (30–60% above current trading prices) represent substantially better economics than post-approval acquisitions at commercial-stage multiples — the Sanofi/Blueprint Medicines \$9.5 billion deal for commercial KIT inhibitor [[7]](https://dealforma.com/large-cap-biopharma-ma-2024-q2-2025/) illustrates the premium cost of waiting. Autoimmune deal-making ranked second only to oncology in 2025, with 106 autoimmune deals (17% of total, up from 76 deals and 10% of total in 2024) and approximately \$48 billion in headline deal value across 29 transactions [[71]](https://www.alacrita.com/whitepapers/autoimmune-disease-drug-development-pipeline-and-biopharma-deals-2026).

**Cell therapy will define the next immunology franchise generation.** CAR-T in autoimmune disease has crossed the clinical validation threshold: SLE patients achieving DORIS remission, SPS patients recovering ambulation, and MG patients achieving drug-free status for over one year [[53]](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/PMC13042968) [[68]](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2308917). The manufacturing cost barrier — approximately \$100,000–\$150,000 per patient and 3–4 week vein-to-vein cycle [[70]](https://www.biospace.com/drug-development/opinion-car-ts-will-only-treat-autoimmune-diseases-if-we-can-scale-delivery) — is being addressed through whole-blood rapid manufacturing (Kyverna Ingenui-T), mRNA engineering eliminating gene integration (Cartesian), and allogeneic off-the-shelf formats (Nkarta, Allogene, CRISPR). An acquirer that waits for Phase 3 proof will face a significantly higher acquisition price.

**Bispecific cytokine blockers are the next monospecific mAb — with the same trajectory.** The global immunology market's shift from IL-12p40 blockers (ustekinumab) to IL-23p19 blockers (risankizumab, guselkumab) to dual-pathway bispecifics (tibulizumab, telitacicept) follows the established pattern of increasing mechanistic precision. An acquirer facing LOE on a monospecific mAb should prioritize bispecific targets (Zura Bio, Vor Bio, Belenos) as direct class successors rather than acquisitions in the same mechanistic category.

BD teams should validate specific LOE dates against company 10-K/20-F filings and FDA Orange Book listings before executing deal timing strategies.
